opening.text: Think of a big family reunion. Cousins come from far away. Some drive all night. Someone is making calls to make sure everyone knows. Someone is holding the door open. And when everyone arrives, there is a lot of hugging. The gathering of Israel is like that. God is calling His children home, and He wants everyone to come.

mainMessage.text: God is gathering His children. Each of us can help, one invitation at a time.

blocks.text: **He is calling** The Lord has long wanted to gather His people. He is still doing it.

O ye people of these great cities which have fallen, who are descendants of Jacob, yea, who are of the house of Israel, how oft have I gathered you as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and have nourished you.
President Russell M. Nelson, President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, said this in his talk “Let God Prevail” from the October 2020 general conference.
The Lord is gathering those who are willing to let God prevail in their lives.
He is still calling.
**Everyone is welcome home** The Father wants all His children to come home. No one is left off the list.
Hear the word of the Lord, O ye nations, and declare it in the isles afar off, and say, He that scattered Israel will gather him, and keep him, as a shepherd doth his flock.
Elder Quentin L. Cook of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Safely Gathered Home” from the April 2023 general conference.
The Father of our spirits desires His children to be safely gathered home.
He wants us all home.
**Who is on the guest list** Being part of Israel is not about where you were born. It is about your covenant with God.
And if ye be Christ’s, then are ye Abraham’s seed, and heirs according to the promise.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Preparing for the Lord’s Return” from the April 2019 general conference.
All who will repent, believe on Christ, and be baptized are His covenant people.
The door is open to all.
**The most important work** The gathering is not a side project. It is central to what God is doing on the earth right now.
And ye are called to bring to pass the gathering of mine elect; for mine elect hear my voice and harden not their hearts;
President Russell M. Nelson, President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, said this in his talk “Let God Prevail” from the October 2020 general conference.
As an essential prelude to the Second Coming of the Lord, it is the most important work in the world!
It matters that much.
**Hold the door open** When someone arrives, the family greets them. We can do that for new members and for those coming back.
Now therefore ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God;
President Russell M. Nelson, President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, said this in his talk “Let God Prevail” from the October 2020 general conference.
We can assist them by welcoming them with open arms and hearts.
Greet them warmly.
**He sets the pace** We don't have to carry the whole reunion alone. The Lord is leading it, and He knows the timing.
Behold, I will hasten my work in its time.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Preparing for the Lord’s Return” from the April 2019 general conference.
It is He who is hastening His work in its time.
He leads, and we help.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they were welcomed in or helped welcome someone else. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: The lost sheep

blocks.text: Jesus told of a shepherd with a hundred sheep. One went missing.

What man of you, having an hundred sheep, if he lose one of them, doth not leave the ninety and nine in the wilderness, and go after that which is lost, until he find it? And when he hath found it, he layeth it on his shoulders, rejoicing. And when he cometh home, he calleth together his friends and neighbours, saying unto them, Rejoice with me; for I have found my sheep which was lost.
The shepherd didn't stop at ninety-nine. And when the one came home, there was a celebration. That is how heaven feels about each person who comes back.

application.text: First, think of someone who might need an invitation. Second, ask them to something simple, like a meal, a service project or a Sunday meeting. Third, greet them kindly when they come.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know God is gathering His children. I know there is a place for every one of us. I know Jesus Christ is the Good Shepherd. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: On a dark night, a lantern on a hill can be seen from miles away. People who are lost turn toward it. They don't have to know the whole road. They just walk toward the light. The gathering of Israel works this way. God sets lights on hills, and His children head for them.

mainMessage.text: God gathers His people toward the light. We can be a lantern for someone who is looking for it.

blocks.text: **The light is lit on purpose** God has been calling His children for a long time. Those who listen move toward Him.

O ye people of these great cities which have fallen, who are descendants of Jacob, yea, who are of the house of Israel, how oft have I gathered you as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and have nourished you.
President Russell M. Nelson, President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, said this in his talk “Let God Prevail” from the October 2020 general conference.
The Lord is gathering those who are willing to let God prevail in their lives.
He lights the way.
**The light is for everyone** The Father wants every child safely home. Every one of us is a person He is looking for.
Hear the word of the Lord, O ye nations, and declare it in the isles afar off, and say, He that scattered Israel will gather him, and keep him, as a shepherd doth his flock.
Elder Quentin L. Cook of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Safely Gathered Home” from the April 2023 general conference.
The Father of our spirits desires His children to be safely gathered home.
His light reaches far.
**Who walks toward it** Anyone who chooses Christ and makes a covenant with Him belongs. Birthplace doesn't decide it.
And if ye be Christ’s, then are ye Abraham’s seed, and heirs according to the promise.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Preparing for the Lord’s Return” from the April 2019 general conference.
All who will repent, believe on Christ, and be baptized are His covenant people.
Anyone can come.
**The work that matters most** This is the work the Lord is doing now. It prepares the world for His return.
And ye are called to bring to pass the gathering of mine elect; for mine elect hear my voice and harden not their hearts;
President Russell M. Nelson, President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, said this in his talk “Let God Prevail” from the October 2020 general conference.
As an essential prelude to the Second Coming of the Lord, it is the most important work in the world!
It is the heart of His work.
**Be a light on the hill** When people find the light, they need a warm place to land. We can offer that.
Now therefore ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God;
President Russell M. Nelson, President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, said this in his talk “Let God Prevail” from the October 2020 general conference.
We can assist them by welcoming them with open arms and hearts.
Offer a warm welcome.
**He keeps the lamp burning** The light isn't ours. It is the Lord's. He keeps it lit and moves the work forward.
Behold, I will hasten my work in its time.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Preparing for the Lord’s Return” from the April 2019 general conference.
It is He who is hastening His work in its time.
The lamp is His.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they felt drawn to the light of the gospel. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: The waters of Mormon

blocks.text: Alma taught in secret, and people came to hear him. At the waters of Mormon, he asked what they were willing to do.

Behold, here are the waters of Mormon (for thus were they called) and now, as ye are desirous to come into the fold of God, and to be called his people, and are willing to bear one another’s burdens, that they may be light; Yea, and are willing to mourn with those that mourn; yea, and comfort those that stand in need of comfort, and to stand as witnesses of God at all times and in all things, and in all places that ye may be in, even until death, that ye may be redeemed of God, and be numbered with those of the first resurrection, that ye may have eternal life— Now I say unto you, if this be the desire of your hearts, what have you against being baptized in the name of the Lord, as a witness before him that ye have entered into a covenant with him, that ye will serve him and keep his commandments, that he may pour out his Spirit more abundantly upon you?
Those people were drawn by the light and asked to share each other's burdens. That is what a gathered people does.

application.text: First, think of one way your life shows the light of Christ. Second, do one thing this week that someone could notice, like a kind word or a small service. Third, be ready to say why.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know God is gathering His people in these days. I know His light is real. I know Jesus Christ is the light of the world. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: A big river begins with many small streams. Each one starts in a different place. Some run down mountains. Some come from far-off valleys. But they all flow in the same direction, and they all end up in the same river. The gathering of Israel is like that. People come from every place, and they flow toward Christ.

mainMessage.text: God is gathering people from every land, like streams flowing into one river. We can help the water find its way.

blocks.text: **The river has a source** The gathering begins with God. He calls, and people respond.

O ye people of these great cities which have fallen, who are descendants of Jacob, yea, who are of the house of Israel, how oft have I gathered you as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and have nourished you.
President Russell M. Nelson, President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, said this in his talk “Let God Prevail” from the October 2020 general conference.
The Lord is gathering those who are willing to let God prevail in their lives.
It starts with Him.
**It flows toward home** A river always runs toward the sea. God's children are being led toward home.
Hear the word of the Lord, O ye nations, and declare it in the isles afar off, and say, He that scattered Israel will gather him, and keep him, as a shepherd doth his flock.
Elder Quentin L. Cook of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Safely Gathered Home” from the April 2023 general conference.
The Father of our spirits desires His children to be safely gathered home.
The current leads home.
**Streams from every place** The streams come from everywhere. What joins them is the covenant, not the place they began.
And if ye be Christ’s, then are ye Abraham’s seed, and heirs according to the promise.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Preparing for the Lord’s Return” from the April 2019 general conference.
All who will repent, believe on Christ, and be baptized are His covenant people.
All streams are welcome.
**The river is the main current** Of all the things happening in the world, this one carries the most weight.
And ye are called to bring to pass the gathering of mine elect; for mine elect hear my voice and harden not their hearts;
President Russell M. Nelson, President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, said this in his talk “Let God Prevail” from the October 2020 general conference.
As an essential prelude to the Second Coming of the Lord, it is the most important work in the world!
It is the main current.
**Clear the way** A river runs best when the channel is open. We can clear the way by welcoming people.
Now therefore ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God;
President Russell M. Nelson, President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, said this in his talk “Let God Prevail” from the October 2020 general conference.
We can assist them by welcoming them with open arms and hearts.
Keep the channel open.
**He controls the flow** We don't make the river run. The Lord does. He knows when it will swell.
Behold, I will hasten my work in its time.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Preparing for the Lord’s Return” from the April 2019 general conference.
It is He who is hastening His work in its time.
He sets the pace.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they felt carried toward God by something bigger than themselves. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Carried on eagles' wings

blocks.text: The people of Israel had been slaves in Egypt. Then God brought them out. He reminded them how.

Ye have seen what I did unto the Egyptians, and how I bare you on eagles’ wings, and brought you unto myself. Now therefore, if ye will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant, then ye shall be a peculiar treasure unto me above all people: for all the earth is mine:
They did not get there on their own. God carried them. And He invited them to keep their covenant. That is still how the gathering works.

application.text: First, think about a time God carried you. Second, share that story with one person who may need to hear it. Third, invite them to try something simple, like reading a scripture or visiting a class.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know God gathers His people from every place. I know He carries us. I know Jesus Christ is the living water. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: A quilt starts as a pile of scraps. Different colors. Different shapes. Some are worn. Some are bright. Alone, none of them look like much. But when someone stitches them together, they make a blanket that keeps a whole family warm. The gathering of Israel is that kind of stitching. God takes people who are very different and makes them one.

mainMessage.text: God is stitching His people together. Each of us is a piece, and each piece matters.

blocks.text: **He holds the needle** The stitching is His work. He calls each of us in, one by one.

O ye people of these great cities which have fallen, who are descendants of Jacob, yea, who are of the house of Israel, how oft have I gathered you as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and have nourished you.
President Russell M. Nelson, President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, said this in his talk “Let God Prevail” from the October 2020 general conference.
The Lord is gathering those who are willing to let God prevail in their lives.
He is doing the stitching.
**He wants every piece** No scrap is thrown out. The Father wants all His children home.
Hear the word of the Lord, O ye nations, and declare it in the isles afar off, and say, He that scattered Israel will gather him, and keep him, as a shepherd doth his flock.
Elder Quentin L. Cook of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Safely Gathered Home” from the April 2023 general conference.
The Father of our spirits desires His children to be safely gathered home.
Every piece counts.
**All kinds of cloth** Silk, cotton and wool can all be in one quilt. In God's family, the thread is the covenant.
And if ye be Christ’s, then are ye Abraham’s seed, and heirs according to the promise.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Preparing for the Lord’s Return” from the April 2019 general conference.
All who will repent, believe on Christ, and be baptized are His covenant people.
The covenant is the thread.
**The quilt is the work** This stitching is the central work of our time.
And ye are called to bring to pass the gathering of mine elect; for mine elect hear my voice and harden not their hearts;
President Russell M. Nelson, President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, said this in his talk “Let God Prevail” from the October 2020 general conference.
As an essential prelude to the Second Coming of the Lord, it is the most important work in the world!
It is the main project.
**Be a steady stitch** Quilts are held by many small stitches. A friendly hello is one. So is a seat saved for someone new.
Now therefore ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God;
President Russell M. Nelson, President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, said this in his talk “Let God Prevail” from the October 2020 general conference.
We can assist them by welcoming them with open arms and hearts.
Small stitches hold.
**He finishes it in His time** A quilt takes time. We don't rush the Maker. He knows when it will be done.
Behold, I will hasten my work in its time.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Preparing for the Lord’s Return” from the April 2019 general conference.
It is He who is hastening His work in its time.
He finishes what He starts.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they felt part of something larger than themselves. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: One heart and one mind

blocks.text: Enoch led a people who learned to live together in peace.
And the Lord called his people Zion, because they were of one heart and one mind, and dwelt in righteousness; and there was no poor among them.
They weren't all the same. But they were united. Being gathered means becoming one, not becoming identical.

application.text: First, think about who feels like an outsider in your ward or circle. Second, sit by them this week. Third, find one thing you have in common and talk about it.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know God is making one people from many. I know every person has a place. I know Jesus Christ is the one who unites us. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: On a cold night, a campfire draws people in. Nobody sends invitations. They see the glow and walk toward it. Someone scoots over to make room. Someone hands over a blanket. Before long, there is a circle. The gathering of Israel feels like this. God lights the fire, and we make room.

mainMessage.text: God lights the fire and calls His children in. We can make room in the circle.

blocks.text: **The fire is His** The gathering is God's work. He is the one calling.

O ye people of these great cities which have fallen, who are descendants of Jacob, yea, who are of the house of Israel, how oft have I gathered you as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and have nourished you.
President Russell M. Nelson, President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, said this in his talk “Let God Prevail” from the October 2020 general conference.
The Lord is gathering those who are willing to let God prevail in their lives.
He lit the fire.
**He wants every seat full** The Father wants all His children safe and warm and home.
Hear the word of the Lord, O ye nations, and declare it in the isles afar off, and say, He that scattered Israel will gather him, and keep him, as a shepherd doth his flock.
Elder Quentin L. Cook of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Safely Gathered Home” from the April 2023 general conference.
The Father of our spirits desires His children to be safely gathered home.
There is a seat for each of us.
**Anyone can sit down** The circle isn't closed. Anyone who chooses Christ and covenants with Him belongs.
And if ye be Christ’s, then are ye Abraham’s seed, and heirs according to the promise.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Preparing for the Lord’s Return” from the April 2019 general conference.
All who will repent, believe on Christ, and be baptized are His covenant people.
No one is turned away.
**The fire matters most** Of all the things we could gather around, this is the one that counts.
And ye are called to bring to pass the gathering of mine elect; for mine elect hear my voice and harden not their hearts;
President Russell M. Nelson, President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, said this in his talk “Let God Prevail” from the October 2020 general conference.
As an essential prelude to the Second Coming of the Lord, it is the most important work in the world!
This is what matters most.
**Scoot over** When someone new steps up to the fire, we make room. We offer a seat, a smile and a blanket.
Now therefore ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God;
President Russell M. Nelson, President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, said this in his talk “Let God Prevail” from the October 2020 general conference.
We can assist them by welcoming them with open arms and hearts.
Make room.
**He tends the fire** We help feed the fire. But the Lord keeps it going and sets the timing.
Behold, I will hasten my work in its time.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Preparing for the Lord’s Return” from the April 2019 general conference.
It is He who is hastening His work in its time.
He keeps it burning.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when someone made room for them, or they made room for someone else. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Peter learns that God welcomes all

blocks.text: Peter had been taught that some people were outside God's circle. Then he visited a Roman soldier named Cornelius, and his view changed.
Then Peter opened his mouth, and said, Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons: But in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him.
Peter saw that God's fire is for everyone. We learn the same. Our job is to make sure no one is left standing in the dark.

application.text: First, think of someone who might feel outside the circle. Second, invite them to join you for something this week. Third, make sure they have a seat and someone to talk to.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know God is gathering all of His children. I know there is room for everyone. I know Jesus Christ is the light we gather around. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.
